message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** Below is a concise guide to some of the most important traffic laws in Texas. For detailed statutes, consult the Texas Transportation Code (TTC) or official state resources. | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• Speed limit signs are typically posted at 5‑mile intervals on highways.
• In construction zones, speed limits may be reduced; failure to obey can result in fines and points. | | **Seat Belt Use** | • All drivers and front-seat passengers must wear seat belts.
• Rear-seat passengers under 15 years old must use a child safety seat or booster.
• Failure to buckle up can lead to a fine and points on your license. | | **DUI / DWI** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal for drivers over 21.
• Lower BAC limits apply to commercial drivers (0.04%) and drivers under 21 (0.02%).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol education, and possible jail time. | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Drivers may only use hands-free devices while operating a vehicle.
• Texting or using a handheld phone while driving is prohibited. | | **Right-of-Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles approaching from the right have priority.
• Pedestrians always have right-of-way at crosswalks. | | **School Bus Rules** | • When a school bus stops and its red lights flash, all vehicles must stop until the lights cease flashing and the bus moves again.
• This applies to both directions of travel. | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be used from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights are allowed only when visibility is less than 1,000 feet. | | **Child Safety Seats** | • Children under 8 years old or weighing less than 40 lbs must use a rear-facing car seat.
• After age 8 or weight 40 lbs, a forward-facing seat is required until age 12 or height 4'9". | | **Parking Regulations** | • Parking on sidewalks, crosswalks, or in front of driveways is prohibited.
• Parking in designated handicap spaces requires a valid handicap placard. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Vehicles must display current registration stickers.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection and emissions test (depending on county). | ### How to Find Specific Statutes - **Texas Transportation Code (TTC)** – The primary source for all traffic laws. You can access it online via the Texas Legislature’s website or through legal research databases. - **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – Offers guides, FAQs, and downloadable handbooks covering driver licensing, vehicle registration, and more. - **Local County Ordinances** – Some counties or cities may impose additional rules (e.g., stricter speed limits, parking restrictions). --- #### Quick Tips for Compliance 1. **Always Observe Posted Signs:** Speed limits, stop signs, yield signs, and other traffic control devices are legally binding. 2. **Use Hands-Free Devices:** If you need to make calls or use navigation, ensure your device is mounted and hands-free. 3. **Check Your Vehicle’s Condition:** Ensure brakes, tires, lights, and mirrors are functioning properly before hitting the road. 4. **Stay Updated on Local Changes:** Roadwork, new signage, or temporary speed limits can change quickly—keep an eye on local news or TxDMV alerts. If you need more detailed information on a specific aspect of Texas traffic law, let me know!
